newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Q4 1996 cocoa grind rises 10.73 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Q4 1996 cocoa grind rises 10.73 pct.

text.p: U.S. 1996 fourth quarter cocoa grindings rose 10.73 percent compared with the same year-ago period to 95,352 tonnes, floor sources said Friday.
The percentage change on grindings reflects a revised 1995 fourth quarter total of 86,116 tonnes, they said. The figure had initially been reported at 93,320 tonnes.
The quantity of liquor melted fell by 31.60 percent versus fourth-quarter 1995 levels to 1,554 tonnes, while the total butter melted slumped 10.60 percent to 15,607 tonnes.
Traders said the grind figures -- which represents the amount of cocoa processed by U.S. manufacturers -- were at the higher than expectations and could offer support to New York cocoa futures.
Analysts had called for an increase of three to five percent.
"I guess it is a little bullish," one trader said. "But I do not know how the liquor and butter numbers will effect the market."
((-- Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk, 212 859 1640))
